question: Can a class-balanced LightGBM model with a cross-validated decision threshold flag failure-prone units better than a standard random forest?
method: Stand-in on OpenML PC4 defect data. Single stratified 75/25 split (seed 42). Baseline: RandomForest (300 trees, threshold 0.5). Improved: balanced LightGBM with 5-fold CV hyperparameter search (ROC-AUC) and CV-F1 threshold, both on training data only. Model seeds 42-44; mean and std reported.
metric_name: F1 for defective class on test split
baseline: Standard scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier (300 trees, default settings, 0.5 decision threshold)
improved: LightGBM with class_weight='balanced'; hyperparameters chosen by 5-fold CV ROC-AUC on the training split; decision threshold chosen by out-of-fold F1 on the training split
notes: Proxy dataset: PC4 static code metrics predict defect-prone modules, not WebRTC test-run failures. Only 45 positives in the test split, so F1 is high-variance; a single split is used. Model seeds vary only model randomness, not the split. Selected LightGBM params: {'learning_rate': 0.03, 'min_child_samples': 5, 'n_estimators': 100, 'num_leaves': 7}; threshold 0.71. The split uses seed 42 (house rule) rather than the seed 0 in the plan. fetch_openml has no timeout argument, so retries wrap the call instead.
